newsitem.title: USA: North Korea hampering its food aid, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: North Korea hampering its food aid, U.S. says.

text.p: North Korea is hindering the international community from giving it desperately needed food by linking other issues to the humanitarian aid, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations Bill Richardson said on Sunday.

"Regrettably North Korea seems to want to link all these issues, and regrettably it prevents the international community from helping them in the area they need most, and that's food aid," Richardson said on the CNN program "Late Edition."

Richardson said the United States was concerned that the Stalinist government in North Korea was not responding to U.S. calls for a joint program to recover Korean War servicemen missing in action for more than 40 years.
North Korea last week also postponed talks with the United States aimed at getting Pyongyang to halt its missile sales to Iran and Syria.

Richardson described food shortages in North Korea as "severe," and said: "Regrettably they're trying to link food aid with a number of other important bilateral issues. The United States very strongly feels that food aid and these other issues need to be separated."
